audit.why: 44.43% over 700 games with an all-Warwick packet chart; full phases[].side and content win[] both read Warwick on all seven rows. The two layers agree, so no flips.

Spike windows are right: his sustain curve starts at level 1 with the passive (heals below 50% health, tripled below 25%), Blood Hunt drops from 80s to 40s with rank, and Infinite Duress lands at 6 on 110/90/70s. Four spike entries present with correct 'when' fields.
audit.corrected: Timings kept; the level 6 mechanics were the error (point 4).

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1].text and mid both call Infinite Duress an 'untargetable leap'. Riot's text says he leaps and suppresses the first champion he collides with for 1.5 seconds — nothing about untargetability, and the kit carries a channel flag meaning the ult is interruptible. The page also omits that Purgatory's grounding denies both Jaws of the Beast and the Infinite Duress leap, since both are dashes.
audit.why: Telling a player he is untargetable during Duress makes them stop trying to answer it. In fact he can be damaged, CC'd out of the channel, and — most usefully here — grounded so the leap never starts.
audit.corrected: Duress described as a 1.5-second suppress off a targetable, interruptible leap; grounding stated as the pre-emptive answer.
sources: enemyKit R text and flags (channel: 'interruptible — any CC cancels it')

audit.why: Grievous Wounds is genuinely mandatory: passive, Q and R all carry heal flags, and the passive's healing triples under 25% health — exactly the range Locke's execute pattern lives in. report[8].t and wants.you[0] already prescribe it early.

edits.before: Infinite Duress (R) is a hard-counter to your execute: it's an untargetable leap into a full-duration suppress, so he locks you down and heals through your Purgatory (R) window before you can finish the threshold.
edits.after: Infinite Duress (R) is a hard counter to your execute: a 1.5-second suppress off a leap that heals him through your threshold. He is not untargetable during it, and Purgatory's grounding stops the leap before it starts — so ult first.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 stay in his favor and 6 is the trap. Infinite Duress is an untargetable leap into a full suppress, which directly answers your execute identity: he locks you, tanks your combo, and heals through your Purgatory before the threshold catches him. Never commit your ult while his R is up. Hold E for the Blood Hunt chase and play for jungle pressure over solo trades.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 stay in his favor and 6 is the trap. Infinite Duress leaps and suppresses you for 1.5 seconds, which answers your execute identity: he locks you, tanks the combo, and heals past your threshold. He is targetable throughout, and Purgatory grounds the leap — so drop it before he jumps, not after. Hold E for the Blood Hunt chase and play for jungle pressure.

edits.before: Late Warwick is a sustain diver who beats your whole gameplan. His passive heals scale with your low HP, his R suppresses through your E blink, and his lifesteal outlasts your single-target burst. Anti-heal is mandatory but not sufficient alone; rely on teammates to peel his Duress and burn his sustain, and only look to execute after his R and heals are spent.
edits.after: Late Warwick is a sustain diver who beats your whole gameplan. His passive healing triples once he is under 25% health, no blink escapes a landed suppress, and his lifesteal outlasts your burst. Anti-heal is mandatory but not sufficient alone; rely on teammates to peel his Duress, and drop Purgatory to ground the leap before he ever reaches you.

edits.before: Never blow Purgatory (R) while his Infinite Duress (R) is available
edits.after: Ground his Infinite Duress (R) leap by dropping Purgatory on him first

notes: Infinite Duress does NOT grant untargetability — the page claimed it twice. It is a channelled suppress and it is interruptible, and both his Q and his R are dashes, so Locke's R grounding is the real answer the page was missing. I changed wants.you[2] as well so it no longer tells the player to hold R while mid tells them to ult first.
